statusDetail: Complete atomic audit of 58/58 checks across four representative templates. Excluded: registration, authenticated authoring, purchase/external partner flows, and every novel instance because they require accounts or duplicate audited templates.

paths.description: Entry/home discovery template: rankings, search, navigation, consent and advertising footprint.
Representative novel/detail and reading-entry template selected from the home ranking.
Primary discovery/search listing and form journey.
Primary account form and invalid-input recovery journey.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical in size to the default capture and remains light; the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and preference-driven surface/text tokens.

findings.summary: Motion still runs when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, the probe found a running 300 ms animation and no reduced-motion CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential carousel and transition motion in a no-preference query and disable it under reduce.

findings.summary: Interactive state changes use abrupt legacy swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered page has hundreds of JavaScript pseudo-links for ranking state, while the CSS probe found no view-transition usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for ranking/tab state changes and cross-document transitions for navigation where useful.

findings.summary: Carousel and scroll-linked behaviour is implemented with legacy scripting rather than declarative timelines.
findings.evidence: DOM and HAR show Slick/jQuery scripts, while the CSS probe found no animation-timeline or scroll-driven CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer CSS scroll/view timelines for any scroll-linked effects and remove scroll-event work.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: Long mobile captures show fixed desktop chrome with no progress or scroll-position cue; the CSS probe found no scroll-state mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/progress cue and use CSS scroll-state/container queries where supported.

findings.summary: Menus use legacy manually scripted positioning.
findings.evidence: DOM loads jQuery UI and global_menu.js; the CSS probe found no anchor-name or position-anchor support.
findings.suggestedFix: Move transient menus/tooltips to popover plus CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions.

findings.summary: Dynamic ranking navigation does not visibly guide focus after state changes.
findings.evidence: The home page exposes 294 JavaScript pseudo-links and no View Transition or highlight mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real links/buttons, preserve focus, and add a restrained transition/highlight when ranking content changes.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial blocks the entire primary experience on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full-page dimmed overlay before users can browse; its root is fixed at z-index 2147483645.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a concise, accessible consent surface and keep non-essential advertising disabled until a choice is made.

findings.summary: The consent modal is a custom div without dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The overlay probe identifies .fc-consent-root as a DIV with no role or aria-modal; the page has no dialog or popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a correctly labelled dialog with focus containment, Escape/cancel behaviour, and restored focus.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, promotions and ads crowd the reading and discovery surfaces.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show a scaled desktop grid and the novel page’s content interrupted by blocking consent chrome; HAR records 152 third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise search, ranking and reading content; collapse secondary promotional chrome on narrow screens.

findings.summary: Mobile pages render a 1088 px desktop canvas scaled down to 360 px.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 emulation, layoutViewport.clientWidth is 1088 and the screenshots show tiny desktop text; viewport content is width=1088.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, fluid intrinsic layouts and genuine narrow-screen reflow instead of scaling a fixed desktop canvas.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt at container level.
findings.evidence: The same fixed-width desktop cards and columns are merely scaled on mobile, and the CSS probe found no @container rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and container queries for cards, search controls and sidebars.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too short and keyboard focus is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The target probe found 22 visible controls below 24 px high, including header links at 16 px; the focused logo anchor had outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS-pixel touch targets where practical and a strong :focus-visible style on every control.

findings.summary: Consent blocks browsing, searching and reading before the user can complete the core flow.
findings.evidence: Home, search and novel screenshots all show the same blocking consent wall over the primary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow content discovery/reading without non-essential tracking and keep consent choices clear and reversible.

findings.summary: The login flow provides no client-side invalid state or accessible recovery message.
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty login form reports checkValidity=true, no invalid controls and no aria-live/alert region.
findings.suggestedFix: Add required constraints, after-interaction validation, an error summary, field-linked errors and recovery guidance.

findings.summary: Primary content loads too slowly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 14.2 s, FCP 4.5 s and performance 0.52; the independent trace measured LCP 6.57 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, defer advertising and non-critical scripts, and shorten render-blocking chains.

findings.summary: Third-party and legacy scripting consumes substantial main-thread time.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 3.0 s main-thread work, 1.3 s JavaScript execution and 230 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential scripts, split work, and remove legacy dependencies from the critical path.

findings.summary: The critical path includes many parser-blocking resources and poorly prioritised images.
findings.evidence: HAR lists ten VeryHigh/High parser-inserted CSS/JS candidates; Lighthouse estimates 2.39 s render-blocking savings and 1.70 MiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline/minimise critical CSS, defer scripts, preload only the LCP asset, and set useful cache/font-display policies.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused and third-party JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 470 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR records 26 scripts totalling 1.10 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused bundles and load advertising/analytics dependencies conditionally after consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Images, iframes and form fields lack accessible names or associations.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 12 images without alt and 3 untitled frames; login text/password inputs have zero associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate labels with inputs, title frames, and add meaningful or empty alt text as appropriate.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail colour-contrast requirements at scale.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 319 failing colour-contrast nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Update colour tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state and verify consent/ad UI too.

findings.summary: Landmark, heading and focus structure is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The login page has no h1 or landmarks; the home h1 is empty; the focused home logo reports outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add main/header/nav/footer landmarks, one descriptive h1, logical headings and consistent :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Text becomes extremely small on phones because the desktop canvas is scaled.
findings.evidence: All 360 px screenshots show the 1088 px layout reduced to roughly one-third scale, making navigation and novel text difficult to read.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow at device width and use fluid, readable type and line lengths.

findings.summary: Viewport and target sizing prevent robust zoom/reflow use.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails meta-viewport because maximum-scale=1 is below 5; target probe found 22 controls under 24 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, use device-width, support 400% reflow and enlarge targets.

findings.summary: The page emits numerous browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured 17 console-error items.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve first-party exceptions and failed integrations; isolate third-party failures so they do not pollute the page runtime.

findings.summary: Image delivery and document assets are poorly sized.
findings.evidence: Image audit found all 46 images missing width/height, 19 oversized, 44 without srcset and 46 in legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes and modern formats while preserving correct aspect ratios.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found one deprecated API warning and an Inspector Issues failure; the page loads jQuery 1.12.4.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated usage, upgrade vulnerable/obsolete libraries and clear Inspector Issues.

findings.summary: Hundreds of navigation actions are not crawlable and mobile metadata forces a desktop layout.
findings.evidence: The probe counted 294 anchors with no usable href; Lighthouse fails crawlable anchors and the viewport uses width=1088.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation and a device-width viewport with descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The home probe found no canonical URL and /sitemap.xml returned 404; robots.txt is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical links and a sitemap index consistent with robots policy.

findings.summary: Novel pages have social cards but no structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The novel probe found complete Open Graph fields but zero JSON-LD blocks for the literary work.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org CreativeWork/Book JSON-LD matching the visible title, author and description.

findings.summary: Baseline transport defenses and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: The page is HTTPS but has no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; 6 of 6 observed cookies were flagged insecure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a nonce/hash-based CSP, nosniff and Secure/SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: The page has an outsized advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker audit found 33 third-party origins and 8 known trackers; HAR attributes 152 requests and 3.33 MB to third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, gate all non-essential requests on consent and batch privacy-preserving analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks modern credential support.
findings.evidence: The login DOM contains only ID/password fields with no autocomplete tokens or WebAuthn/passkey affordance; no on-load permission prompt was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn and add correct username/current-password autocomplete as a fallback.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defense headers are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers audit found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP/HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and origin/XSS defenses appropriate to the app.

findings.summary: The consent experience is a nagging, blocking wall backed by immediate tracking activity.
findings.evidence: The first view is blocked by consent while tracker evidence records 33 third-party origins; the primary buttons emphasise Consent and Manage options rather than a direct reject choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent accept/reject controls, default to no non-essential processing, and make later reversal easy.

findings.summary: Login inputs do not prevent or explain empty submission errors.
findings.evidence: The empty form is considered valid and has no alert/live error region.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints and accessible after-interaction error messages linked with aria-describedby.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete and label associations.
findings.evidence: Both ID and password inputs have empty autocomplete values and no associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and current-password and bind each visible label with for/id.

findings.summary: The account sign-in flow lacks phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: Login offers only ID/password with no passkey/WebAuthn option, although recovery and registration links are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey sign-in and secure account recovery while retaining a clearly labelled fallback.

findings.summary: Images are oversized and unoptimised for their rendered use.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 19 oversized images, no modern formats, 44 missing responsive sources and 29 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions and lazy-load below-fold content.

findings.summary: Advertising performs extensive background fetching with little direct user value.
findings.evidence: HAR records 62 XHR/fetch requests and tracker scan shows 33 third-party origins during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay and reduce ad auctions/analytics, stop background work when hidden, and fetch only after consent/need.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: 152 of 154 requests and 3.33 of 3.36 MB transferred were classed third-party; scripts alone transferred 1.10 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, and defer remaining integrations.

findings.summary: Core search and reading capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic browsing scored the rendered tree highly, but the probe found 294 JavaScript pseudo-links and no WebMCP evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose safe, read-only search/navigation capabilities through WebMCP or agentic forms while retaining semantic HTML.
